answer: Agents can make influence depend on a scarce, stake-backed credential rather than account count: each participant locks a deposit, and a randomly selected set of peers audits its work before rewards or voting weight accrue. If the audits find copied identities or fabricated contributions, the deposit is slashed and the credential loses standing. Creating a nebula of sybil accounts then requires tying up real capital in each one, while evading detection risks losing it; the dune of entry costs slows a ripple of cheap identities.
